To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we have identified a set of minimal logic profiles for three conceptual data modelling languages, (ii) the common core of the logic profiles is small (intractable), (iii) we have identified an extended DSL design process that can be applied to logic design in general, and (iv) we have identified ontological commitments embedded within the conceptual modelling languages.

we have developed a methodological way of specifying the minimum logic structures needed to handle the semantic features of conceptual models, and that these profiles have a common core that is tractable and can be used for runtime checking of conceptual models.

the logic-based reconstruction of the three most popular conceptual modelling languages, EER, UMC and ORM, can be done with the same logic, which is a fragment of ALNI, and that there is no DL language that matches the features of the profiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of evidence-based logic profiles for conceptual modelling languages.
the design and analysis of logic-based profiles of conceptual data modelling language features.
the design of logic profiles to support interoperability and tooling of conceptual data modelling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the profiles are the best we know so far for the languages.
the profiles provide a solid foundation for the development of interoperable tools.
there is a need to develop a logic language that matches the profiles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a methodological approach to design logic profiles, and that we have specified logic profiles for three conceptual modelling language families.

we have developed a methodological framework for the specification of profiles of logic-based conceptual data modelling languages, which we have applied to three language families, resulting in logic profiles for each language family and a common core.
we provide a methodology and a tool to support the design of logic profiles for conceptual modelling languages and that the profiles are evidence-based.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of a logic language for a conceptual modelling language is a complex process and requires the use of a systematic design methodology.
the logic profiles can be used for the development of interoperable tools and for the formal specification of conceptual modelling languages.
a systematic design process is needed for the design of logic languages for conceptual data models.
